messages.author: c581d1960852c8a3
messages.subject: design question
parts:
Hi list,
we are planning a line survey to estimate roe deer densities in 9 different forest patches.
The main aim of the study is to compare densities of deer among areas (and later on to compare estimates over time).
Since we have to conduct the study at night and by vehicle, the survey design needs to be restricted to forest roads.
In 4 areas, it is possible to distribute 15-20 transects systematically over each forest.
However, in the other 5 areas, the terrain is rather hilly and hence the roads are not distributed systematically but rather follow contour lines. Actually, the roads form "roundtrips". Within each area, the tracks are quite evenly distributed but it is not possible to identify single roads which could be used as a proxy for a transect.
Would it be ok to treat every new km of a roundtrip as a "new" transect or how (if at all) can one split the whole road network in suitable transects?

I know that the entire road-design approach bears serious design-based inference problems but maybe someone has a good idea to make the best out off a difficult setting?

Kind regards,

Christian
